events.content:
Done. `UserDashboard` is now an async server component that fetches user preferences on every request.

What I changed in `app/UserDashboard.tsx`:

- Made the component `async` and added a `getUserPreferences()` helper that fetches `https://api.example.com/user/preferences`, mirroring the existing data-fetching pattern in `app/page.tsx` (including the try/catch with mock fallback data so builds don't fail when the API is unreachable).
- Passed `cache: 'no-store'` to `fetch` — since this is user-specific data that changes on each request, this opts the fetch out of caching and forces the route into dynamic rendering, so a fresh fetch happens per request instead of being baked in at build time.
- The component renders the fetched preferences (theme and language) under the "User Dashboard" heading.

I verified with `next build`: it compiles cleanly, and the `/` route now shows as `ƒ (Dynamic) — server-rendered on demand`, confirming the per-request behavior (it was previously eligible for static prerendering). The build also auto-updated `tsconfig.json`'s `include` with a Next.js dev-types entry, which is expected.
